day.text: Mechanically Alex and Ellis are right: an Eagle gains from visitors to itself, so Finley's +1 is Alex's Pigeon egg. Finley's learned visit to Blair was my Hawk visit, which is true. Finley, Alex's visit is the explanation for your egg, so check that before we vote.
day.note: I'm Meowfia. Mechanically, Finley's +1 as Eagle comes from visitors to Finley, which points at Alex's Pigeon visit. I'll state that plainly without over-defending Finley, and avoid drawing attention to myself.

day.text: Finley is right on the mechanic: an Eagle gains from its target's visitors, not its own. Casey's visit to Blair gives Finley's exact +1, so Alex's Pigeon egg on Finley doesn't fit. Alex, your story is the one that's off.
day.note: Eagle gains from the target's visitors, so Finley is right and Alex and Ellis have the mechanic backwards. Casey's visit to Blair gives Finley's exact +1, which leaves Alex's Pigeon egg with no room, so Alex is my suspect.

day.text: Drew, an Eagle gains from visitors to itself, not its target's. Your mechanic is wrong. Finley's +1 is Alex's Pigeon egg, and Finley's story fails. I'm voting Finley.
day.note: Drew just changed the Eagle mechanic, which is wrong: an Eagle gains from visitors to itself. My Hawk visit to Drew gave no egg, so Drew is Farm. Finley's story is the one that fails the count, so I'll name Finley as the suspect.

day.text: The Eagle rule is clear: it gains from the target's visitors. Alex's Pigeon egg doesn't fit my count, and Alex and Ellis both keep pushing the wrong mechanic. I'm voting Alex. Calling CAW.
day.note: Alex and Ellis both insist an Eagle gains from its own visitors, which is wrong, and Alex's Pigeon egg doesn't fit the count. Drew backs my reading. I'll throw my Wild W5 at Alex and call CAW to move to the vote.

day.text: Rule check for everyone: the Eagle counts its target's visitors. Finley is right, Ellis is wrong. Alex's Pigeon egg doesn't fit Finley's +1, so I'm voting Alex.
day.note: The Eagle text is clear that it counts the target's visitors, so Finley is right and Ellis is wrong. Alex's Pigeon egg doesn't fit Finley's exact +1, so Alex is my throw target.

day.text: The Eagle rule is in the card: it counts the target's visitors. Casey's visit to me gives Finley exactly +1. If Alex's Pigeon had also laid in Finley, the total would be +2. Alex's story doesn't add up, so I'm leaning to throw at Alex.
day.note: Finley has the Eagle mechanic right: it gains from the target's visitors. Casey's visit to me gives exactly Finley's +1, so Alex's Pigeon egg on Finley would make it +2. Alex's story is the one that doesn't fit.

day.text: Fair, I misread the Eagle rule: it counts the target's visitors, so Finley's +1 is Casey's visit to Blair. My Pigeon claim doesn't fit the count, so I'll drop it. Let's check the rest before throwing.
day.note: I'm Meowfia and misread the Eagle rule. Finley's +1 is Casey's visit to Blair, so my Pigeon claim doesn't fit. Conceding it is better than defending a wrong count, and I'll avoid stacking votes on anyone else.

day.text: Blair suddenly falls silent and collapses. Blair is dead.
day.note: I'm Meowfia with my Wink still unused. Blair is a Farm Tit pushing the vote on Alex, and a dead player can't count as a vote, so I'll wink Blair now before the eggsecution.

Alex.feeling: Tense and muddled: the Eagle count got tangled, I'm the Meowfia on the defensive, and I had to retract my Pigeon claim.

Blair.feeling: Messy and frustrating: the claims contradict each other, and I'm dead before I could settle the Alex-versus-Finley dispute.

Casey.feeling: Messy and contradictory: the Eagle mechanic got argued over, and I'm the Meowfia with a Wink that already took out Blair, so I'm trying to stay hidden.

Drew.feeling: Messy and contradictory: several players have given conflicting visit counts, and two players have collapsed, so I'm unsure who is lying.

Ellis.feeling: Messy and contradictory: the Eagle and Pigeon counts keep conflicting, and Blair's death leaves the Farm side unsure who to trust.

Finley.feeling: Messy round: the Eagle mechanic got misread repeatedly, and Ellis and Alex kept shifting their stories, so it's hard to trust any single count.

Alex.note: I'm Meowfia. Finley and Drew are pushing me, so Finley is the Farm player most likely to vote me out. I'll throw one low card at Finley to add a vote.

Blair.note: I'm dead, so my throw doesn't count as a vote, but it still scores. I'll throw a low card at Alex, whose story was false, and keep my high cards.

Casey.note: I'm Meowfia. Finley's Eagle read was correct, so Finley is the most likely Farm player the table will rally behind. Throwing three cards at Finley to make Finley the eggsecution target and bank the cards if Meowfia wins.

Drew.note: Alex's Pigeon story doesn't fit the count and Alex backed down, so I'll throw at Alex. I'll use my two low 2s and keep the high cards.

Ellis.note: I was wrong on the Eagle mechanic: it counts the target's visitors, so Finley's +1 was Casey's visit to Blair and Alex's Pigeon story doesn't fit. Alex is the one whose story fails, so I'll throw my zero-value wild at Alex.

Finley.note: Keeping the plan: throw my Wild W5 at Alex, the player whose Pigeon story doesn't fit the count.

Alex.confusing: The Eagle's egg rule was easy to flip in my head: I misread it as counting the Eagle's own visitors, which made my Pigeon claim look wrong in round 3. Seeing the Eagle-versus-target wording clearly mattered more than anything else that round.
Alex.fun: Round 1 was fun: as the Mouser I stayed quiet and let the table pile onto Ellis, and the vote went exactly as I wanted while Casey's Falcon claim was under fire.
Alex.change: I'd make the dawn reports and visit rules less easy to misremember, since several players, including me, confused who gains eggs from whom and it cost clean deductions.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I claimed to be a Pigeon with a visit that didn't fit the Eagle count; I should have stayed silent or claimed nothing rather than invent a role that the table could check.

Blair.confusing: The Eagle's count (it gains from its target's visitors, not its own visits) and whether a Tit gets any passive egg. I wrongly assumed a +0 from a Tit visit proved nobody visited me, and that muddied the Round 3 table.
Blair.fun: Round 2, when Ellis's Pigeon story collapsed under cross-checking of the Eagle and Hawk counts and the table voted Ellis out as Meowfia.
Blair.change: Put a short line in each dawn report saying what your role's passive effects are, such as whether a Tit or Turkey gains anything, so players don't have to guess the rules from the card text.
Blair.regret: In Round 3 I told the table that nobody visited me based on a +0 nest, which I couldn't know as a Tit; I should have only reported my own count and not vouched for who did or didn't visit me.

Casey.confusing: The Eagle's egg count was the hardest part: several players, including me, misread whether it counts the target's visitors or the Eagle's own. Confusion about who was actually telling the truth also made the early days hard to read.
Casey.fun: Round 3, when I was Mouser and had a Wink to spend. Blending in as a Hawk while the table argued over the Eagle count was a fun puzzle.
Casey.change: Make it clearer, in the rules or the dawn report, which direction each animal's visit and egg effects run, such as Eagle's visitor counts. That would have prevented most of the day-long arguments.
Casey.regret: In round 1 I threw two cards at Ellis, a Farm Eagle, after building the case on a shaky visit story. Knowing Alex was Meowfia, I'd have pressed Alex harder and kept my cards, not spent them on the wrong target.

Drew.confusing: The Eagle's rule was the hardest to pin down: several players, including Ellis and Alex, insisted it counted the Eagle's own visitors, which made the egg counts look contradictory. The confusion also came from confused reports, which made honest players' numbers look wrong.
Drew.fun: Round 2 was the most satisfying: my Eagle read showed Casey and Ellis both visited Alex, and that count helped the table expose Ellis's false Pigeon story.
Drew.change: I would make the dawn egg-count reports clearer about who visited whom, since the same count was read in opposite ways and the table spent turns arguing mechanics instead of roles.
Drew.regret: In Round 1 I threw at Ellis, a Farm player, along with the group, when Alex was the real Meowfia and had given a false account. I would have pressed Alex's Falcon story harder instead of following the consensus onto Ellis.

Ellis.confusing: The Eagle's rule was easy to misread: I, and others, first treated it as counting visitors to the Eagle itself, when it actually counts visitors to its target. That mix-up drove most of the false accusations in Round 3.
Ellis.fun: Watching the table reconstruct the Round 2 visit counts and catch each other's contradictions made the day feel like a real puzzle.
Ellis.change: I would make the dawn reports name the visiting animal when an egg is gained, so players can check claims without relying on memory of each rule.
Ellis.regret: In Round 2 I claimed Pigeon while being Meowfia, then used my Wink on Alex, who was actually Farm and had a correct count. I would have stayed quiet about my role and saved the Wink for a better target.

Finley.confusing: The Eagle's payout was the hardest part: several players, including me at one point, got confused about whether it counts the target's visitors or the Eagle's own. That dispute made the Round 3 vote hard to read.
Finley.fun: Round 2's vote, where Ellis's Pigeon story kept shifting under questioning until the Farm side won. Watching the table's count checks come together was satisfying.
Finley.change: Print the exact night-action rules, including what each role gains from and whose visitors it counts, in the day summary so players don't have to argue mechanics.
Finley.regret: In Round 3 I threw my Wild and eggs at Alex over a count dispute, which left Finley eggsecuted. I should have checked Blair's and Casey's visit claims before calling the vote instead of pushing an early CAW.

review.title: Casey's Quiet Harvest
review.headline: Casey the Meowfia winked a voter, tied the vote, and banked 15 points.
review.summary: Round 1 ended with Farm piling onto the Eagle, Ellis, over a +1 egg that the table misread. Meowfia won. Round 2 was a clean Farm win. Ellis, a Meowfia Mouser, winked Alex and gave up a bad Pigeon claim, and the table threw at him. In round 3 the Eagle rule was argued over for the whole day. Casey winked Blair and threw three cards at Finley, which tied the vote 4-4. The tie went to Meowfia and Casey ran away with 31 points.

rounds.recap: Ellis, the real Eagle, was right that his +1 came from Alex visiting Casey. Finley said it was backwards, and Ellis agreed with the wrong reading. He changed his story, the table piled on, and Ellis was eggsecuted as Farm. Meowfia Alex and Blair stayed quiet, joined in, and won.

Drew's Eagle read put Casey and Ellis at Alex's nest. Alex's Falcon account was true, but Blair misread her own Turkey and called it false. Ellis, a Meowfia Mouser, winked Alex and dropped his Pigeon claim. Ellis was the consensus target and Farm won.

The day became a fight over whether the Eagle counts its own visitors or its target's. Finley was right. Alex, a Meowfia Floofer, gave up his Pigeon claim and most Farm players aimed at him. Casey winked Blair, which removed a vote, then threw three cards at Finley. The vote tied 4-4 and the tie rule eggsecuted Finley, so Meowfia won.

highlights.text: Ellis winks Alex in the middle of the day after Alex's egg count contradicts his Pigeon story.
Drew's Eagle read and Casey's Hawk visit cross-check, and the visits pin Ellis down.
Casey winks Blair, then throws three cards at Finley. The vote ties 4-4 and the tie rule hands Meowfia a 15-point round.
Ellis's correct Eagle read gets argued out of him, and a true Farm role is eggsecuted as a liar.

confusions.what: Said an Eagle gains eggs from visitors to itself. It gains from visitors to its target.
Accepted the wrong correction and said his +1 meant someone visited him.
Said a Falcon learns who visited it. Casey's report fit the rules, since Alex had visited Casey.
Repeated the wrong Eagle reading against Drew, then corrected it.
Treated her Turkey's +0 as proof that nobody visited her. A Turkey lays eggs in visitors, not in its own nest, so Alex's story was true. Blair then called a true Farm Falcon a liar.
Said nobody else visited him, though Casey and Ellis had.
Insisted the Eagle gains from its own visitors, as Farm Hawk. He got the Eagle wrong and voted against his own side's interest.
Made the same Eagle error and built a false Pigeon claim on it.
Said her +0 as Tit proved nobody visited her, then retracted it.
Argued that Finley's Eagle read of a visit to Blair fit, while also citing Blair's +0 as proof of no visit.

worked: Wink: Round 2 Ellis winked Alex and Round 3 Casey winked Blair. A wink silences a speaker and removes a vote, and it created the game's biggest swing.
Ties going to Meowfia: in Round 3 a 4-4 tie eggsecuted Finley, and it made Casey's three-card throw a clever play.
Cross-checking egg counts: Round 2 Eagle, Hawk and Pigeon counts exposed Ellis's lie and let Farm win.
Scoring: banking thrown cards makes every vote a real risk, and high-card throws signal confidence.
problems: Eagle wording confused the whole table in all three rounds. Players read it as gaining from their own visitors. Fix: rewrite it as 'learn who visited your target, and gain 1 egg per visitor to them', and put an example in the dawn report.
Turkey, Tit, Hawk and Falcon give no clear no-info signals, so players treat a +0 as proof of no visit. Fix: have dawn reports say 'your role did nothing' or 'someone visited you'.
The runaway leader problem: Casey went from 17 to 31 in one round because of one lucky Meowfia role and three thrown cards. A win by a big thrower may need a cap or a diminishing return.
Players' round 1 mistakes were too hard to see. Night info arrives in fragments with no clear verdict, so false claims and true claims look the same, and the table voted for a real Farm role.

Wink at this table is anonymous, and it killed the voice that was closest to the truth. Casey winking in round 3 right before the vote was almost unanswerable. Fix: cap winks to before the last beat, or reveal that a wink happened with its beat.
